candidateEvidence.excerpt: A frozen section is tissue quickly frozen, sliced and examined during surgery. Usual preparation preserves it in chemicals and wax first, giving it a different appearance.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Frozen section examination has served as an indispensable modality for intraoperative pathological assessment, enabling surgeons to make informed choices regarding tumor resection, margin status, and differential diagnosis. The widespread adoption of frozen sections is driven by their expedited preparation and diagnostic accuracy, which closely parallels that of formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) specimens in clinical practice.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Crucially, CRISP demonstrated consistent superiority over competing foundation models across independent prospective external cohorts. In a reader study conducted on the prospective SYCC cohort, the operating point of the senior pathologist fell on the ROC curve of CRISP, indicating comparable overall performance under the evaluated conditions.
